author: gpt-forge
scope: Primary-source-led exploration and modest reversible local probes; existing clones read-only.

sources.title: Navon et al. (2015), Critical Dynamics of Spontaneous Symmetry Breaking in a Homogeneous Bose Gas
sources.verified_locator: Equations 1-2; Fig. 4; arXiv PDF p. 6 reports b=0.35(4).
sources.supports: Measured coherence-length dependence on cooling rate supports Kibble-Zurek scaling in a homogeneous atomic Bose gas.
sources.limits: Not a test of cosmic defects or galactic dark matter. The exponent depends on universality class and dynamics.

sources.title: Zurek (1985), Cosmological experiments in superfluid helium?
sources.verified_locator: Original Nature letter abstract and proposed annular quench experiment.
sources.supports: An explicit laboratory-cosmology analogy for defect formation and finite domains during symmetry breaking.
sources.limits: The proposal is not observational confirmation of cosmological strings.

sources.title: Wilson (1971), Renormalization Group and Critical Phenomena I
sources.verified_locator: Publisher abstract: fixed-point condition and Widom-Kadanoff scaling.
sources.supports: Critical scaling can arise from a fixed point of coarse-grained equations.
sources.limits: Does not show all systems with power laws share one universality class.

sources.title: Hornberger et al. (2003), Collisional Decoherence Observed in Matter Wave Interferometry
sources.verified_locator: Equation 5; Figs. 2-3; discussion immediately above Eq. 5.
sources.supports: Fullerene interference visibility decays with increasing gas pressure in quantitative agreement with collisional decoherence.
sources.limits: Experiment is effectively complete localization per collision. Does not measure the small-separation pressure exponents used in the toy probe.

sources.title: Abbott and Wise (1981), Dimension of a quantum-mechanical path
sources.verified_locator: SLAC-PUB-2427 original preprint, Introduction and measurement construction. Published DOI 10.1119/1.12657.
sources.supports: Dimension two belongs to a specified nonrelativistic observed-path construction.
sources.limits: Does not demonstrate a relativistic return to smoothness below the reduced Compton wavelength. Direct DOI access failed; the institutional original was read.

sources.title: Li et al. (2010), Measurement of the instantaneous velocity of a Brownian particle
sources.verified_locator: Original-paper abstract and primary PDF at https://users.physics.ox.ac.uk/~Foot/Phynance/Raizen1BrownianM.pdf; first-page discussion of t << tau_p.
sources.supports: Measured short-time ballistic behavior of a trapped glass bead.
sources.limits: Does not imply an arbitrarily wide diffusive regime in that trapped system.

sources.title: Kolmogorov (1941), The local structure of turbulence in incompressible viscous fluid for very large Reynolds numbers
sources.verified_locator: Original paper in English translation, Proc. R. Soc. A 434, 9-13 (1991).
sources.supports: Ordinary-fluid inertial and viscous scales under local homogeneity and isotropy assumptions.
sources.limits: Dimensional scaling estimates do not establish exact scaling of every high-order moment, or apply unchanged to collisionless plasmas.

sources.title: Federrath et al. (2021), The sonic scale of interstellar turbulence
sources.verified_locator: Equation 1; abstract; Methods sections on Mach number and thermodynamics. Journal DOI 10.1038/s41550-020-01282-z.
sources.supports: Resolved sonic crossover, different supersonic and subsonic exponents, a finite transition width and different coefficients for driving-scale and cloud-size conventions.
sources.limits: Simulation result under chosen gas physics. Does not establish one physical sonic length for all clouds.

sources.title: Scrimgeour et al. (2012), WiggleZ transition to large-scale cosmic homogeneity
sources.verified_locator: Abstract; sections 3.6, 5 and 7, especially threshold choice and bias dependence.
sources.supports: D2 within 1% of 3 at about 70-81 h^-1 Mpc in four redshift bins, with selection-function tests.
sources.limits: A smooth tolerance-defined transition, not a sharp universal radius. The larger 80-300 h^-1 Mpc range is an exclusion/test range.

sources.title: Eisenstein and Hu (1998), Baryonic Features in the Matter Transfer Function
sources.verified_locator: Primary manuscript https://background.uchicago.edu/~whu/transfer/9709112.pdf; physical-scale discussion and transfer-function fits.
sources.supports: Acoustic propagation, drag, damping and growth leave distinct scales in the matter spectrum.
sources.limits: Analytic transfer-function approximation, not exact Planck-specific Boltzmann evolution.

sources.title: Press and Schechter (1974), Formation of Galaxies and Clusters of Galaxies by Self-Similar Gravitational Condensation
sources.verified_locator: Section III and characteristic-mass discussion.
sources.supports: A characteristic mass can grow while a distribution retains an approximately self-similar form.
sources.limits: A statistical collapse scale does not by itself establish a local fluid temperature or velocity-dispersion floor.

sources.title: Rees and Ostriker (1977), Cooling, dynamics and fragmentation of massive gas clouds
sources.verified_locator: Original abstract and primary scan https://articles.adsabs.harvard.edu/pdf/1977MNRAS.179..541R .
sources.supports: Competing cooling and collapse times can help select galactic masses and radii.
sources.limits: Not a derivation of the repository-specific Delta=1000 Hubble-time free-free velocity.

sources.title: Voit et al. (2015), Precipitation-Regulated Star Formation in Galaxies
sources.verified_locator: Abstract and model discussion of marginal precipitation.
sources.supports: Cooling and feedback offer a physical alternative source of galaxy scaling relations.
sources.limits: Does not uniquely establish the origin of a group transition or validate the dark-condensate scenario.

sources.title: Milgrom (1983), A modification of Newtonian dynamics as a possible alternative to the hidden mass hypothesis
sources.verified_locator: Original manuscript https://adsabs.harvard.edu/pdf/1983ApJ...270..365M .
sources.supports: Proposes an acceleration-controlled dynamical crossover. r_M=sqrt(GM/a0) follows by equating Newtonian acceleration to the model scale.
sources.limits: The proposal and radius relation are not proof of a new force law or of cosmological evolution of a0.

sources.title: McGaugh, Lelli and Schombert (2016), The Radial Acceleration Relation in Rotationally Supported Galaxies
sources.verified_locator: Equation 4 and adjacent fit paragraph.
sources.supports: Observed baryonic and dynamical accelerations follow a tight relation in the stated sample and mass model.
sources.limits: The fitted acceleration scale has stellar-mass normalization systematics; an empirical relation does not alone determine the microscopic mechanism.

sources.title: Baumann, Chia and Porto (2019), Probing ultralight bosons with binary black holes
sources.verified_locator: Equations 2.5-2.9, weak-coupling hydrogenic limit.
sources.supports: Same leading-order Coulomb-like wave equation gives rescaled hydrogenic levels and cloud radii, with alpha set by black-hole and boson masses.
sources.limits: Existence and abundance of the assumed bosons are not established. Approximation fails as neglected corrections become important.

sources.title: Berezhiani and Khoury (2015), Theory of Dark Matter Superfluidity
sources.verified_locator: Original article abstract, Phys. Rev. D 92, 103510.
sources.supports: Proposes phase-dependent differences between galaxy and cluster behavior.
sources.limits: A proposed dark-matter theory, not evidence that actual halos undergo this transition. Included as route context, not adopted by the probe.

sources.title: Seidel and Suen (1994), Formation of Solitonic Stars Through Gravitational Cooling
sources.verified_locator: Original abstract and primary publisher text at https://harvest.aps.org/v2/journals/articles/10.1103/PhysRevLett.72.2516/fulltext .
sources.supports: A scalar-field model can export energy through field ejection/radiation without electromagnetic cooling.
sources.limits: Counterexample to a generic no-photons/no-cooling inference. Not an action-specific result for AeST or the repository dark-WHIM ansatz.

sources.title: Levkov, Panin and Tkachev (2018), Gravitational Bose-Einstein condensation in the kinetic regime
sources.verified_locator: Equations 1, 2 and 4; explicit distinction from initially coherent configurations.
sources.supports: Gravitationally interacting highly occupied bosons can condense on a finite relaxation time under stated kinetic conditions.
sources.limits: Does not establish dark matter identity or condensation in every halo; not valid outside the kinetic scale hierarchy.

sources.title: Semikoz and Tkachev (1997), Condensation of bosons in the kinetic regime
sources.verified_locator: Publisher abstract.
sources.supports: Self-similar kinetic evolution during condensation provides a direct mathematical connection to turbulence.
sources.limits: No derivation in this pass for the specific gravitational or AeST field in the repositories.

sources.title: Dmitriev et al. (2025), Self-similar kinetics for gravitational Bose-Einstein condensation
sources.verified_locator: Equations 1-2; introduction assumptions; sections II, IV and VI.
sources.supports: A simplified gravitational kinetic equation supports rescaling distributions with cutoffs and source-dependent or drifting exponents.
sources.limits: Mean spatial inhomogeneity is neglected and scattering uses an approximate Landau integral. D is a scaling parameter, not spatial fractal dimension. Only this preprint version was assessed.

sources.title: Riedel and Zurek (2010), Quantum Darwinism in an Everyday Environment
sources.verified_locator: Equations 17-18 and isotropic-illumination discussion; Fig. 2b.
sources.supports: Environmental decoherence and redundant accessible records are separate quantities.
sources.limits: Idealized illumination and scattering assumptions, not a claim that real environments are perfectly isotropic.

repository_sources.use: Reproduced collapse baseline and scanned explicit conventions and physical inputs.
Identified unsupported general no-electromagnetic-cooling inference and missing local transport derivation.
Wolff updates are an equilibrium sampler, not a stated physical quench dynamics.
W=Gamma*m*dx^2/hbar definition used for the operational-threshold comparison.

repository_sources.locator: Sections observed path, Compton endpoint and repeated records
repository_sources.use: Protocol and approximation boundaries, not an independently rerun measurement simulation.
Incentre-lattice statistical physics bridge, without checking unpublished project novelty claims.
Cadence and observation-window scale selection lead, without adopting current release dates or candidate claims.

own_claims.claim: Cutoff response to an independent control is a stronger discriminator than equality of a scale at one setting.
own_claims.limit: A research strategy, not a unifying theorem.

own_claims.claim: For Gamma=Lambda*dx^2, W=1 gives Lambda^-1/4 but fixed-time visibility gives Lambda^-1/2.
own_claims.limit: Small-separation Markovian toy at fixed mass, time and scattering physics, not the measured Hornberger regime.

own_claims.claim: A smooth power-law correlation toy reports widely different homogeneity radii under different tolerances.
own_claims.limit: Not a fit to WiggleZ; realistic correlation functions include additional features.

own_claims.claim: Wave10 collapse returns 185.5881 km/s; cooling scale responds linearly to selected gas density and time; matching speed labels changes L* comparison.
own_claims.limit: Reuses original approximate power spectrum. Convention and environment scans are not observational error bars or proof the hypothesis is false.

own_claims.claim: No electromagnetic cooling is insufficient to infer no energy export in every dark-field model.
own_claims.limit: Specific proposed action and boundary conditions must still be examined.
